recipes.name: Easy Sausage Gravy and Biscuits
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) can refrigerated jumbo buttermilk biscuits
1 (9.6 ounce) package Jimmy Dean® Original Hearty Pork Sausage Crumbles
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Arrange biscuits 1 to 2 inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet. Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 13 to 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook sausage in a large skillet over medium heat until thoroughly heated, stirring frequently, about 5 to 6 minutes.
Stir in flour until well combined.
Gradually add milk, stirring continuously, until the gravy thickens and comes to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer and stir for 2 more minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Split biscuits in half. Place 2 halves on each of 8 plates; top with about 1/3 cup gravy.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Sausage Gravy and Biscuits
raw_recipe.description: This biscuits and gravy recipe with refrigerated jumbo biscuits and homemade creamy sausage gravy is ready in just 15 minutes for a hearty breakfast.

video.description: In this video, learn how to make easy sausage and gravy biscuits. First, bake the jumbo buttermilk biscuits at 350 degrees for around 15 minutes. Next, cook the pork sausage over medium heat for around 5-6 minutes. Finally, prepare the gravy using flour and milk combined with the sausage in the pan. Add a little salt and pepper for some extra taste. Start the morning with this delicious and flavorful recipe.

review.reviewBody: This is a great basic Sausage and Gravy! My husband grew up eating this stuff and introduced it to me about 10 years ago. It is a family staple now. A note on the gravy: DO NOT DRAIN THE SAUSAGE. You need the grease inorder to bring the gravy together, adding butter will drastically change the flavor. We use red pepper flakes and toss it in as the sausage is cooking. You can also use the "hot" flavored sausage to get an extra layer of flavor. Make sure that you completly stir in the flour and alow it to cook with the sausage and grease for a minute or two before addin the milk, this will take out any "pastey taste". Add the milk slowly, I have used skim, 1%, all the way to cream, usually whatever I have on hand. I have found that the less fat your milk has, the less milk you will need to create the gravy! Great on biscuts, toast, cornbread, mashed potatoes, and more...yummmm :)

I didn't have Jimmy Dean crumbles but I did have a roll of the ground sausage I used. I couponed a couple days ago and had a few canisters of whomp biscuits so this was perfect for that. I did add a little red pepper flake. Whole skillet? Gone. Great winter snowy morning breakfast. NOTE: For most white gravy mixes, I use equal amounts butter and flour and make a roux in the skillet before I wisk in the milk. It makes for a better gravy.

First time making sausage gravy. Store only had Jimmy Dean Turkey Sausage Crumbles, so I opted for that. Added a little butter to the pan for grease factor so the flour would stick. I made sure the flour was on all the turkey sausage before pouring the milk in. Followed the rest of the directions for cooking. Seasoned with salt, pepper, garlic, and a little crushed red pepper. Used Pillsbury Buttery Biscuits. Turned out perfect.
First time I made this on a craving whim at 2am. Smelled so good it rose the husband out of bed! It's really good, needs a tad bit more flour than 1/4 cup but maybe that's just me?
Replaced 1/2 cup milk with heavy cream and cooked the flour for a few minutes before adding milke. Delicious!!

I have had this both with and without butter. I agree with Jim Thomas, this is much better with 1/4 butter (I used salted). I also "doubled" the sausage - using 1 lb pkg of Jimmy Dean Hot breakfast sausage. I also simmered for almost 5 minutes to get the thick gravy I love.

I bought canned sausage gravy and my husband made homemade buttermilk biscuits, but I didn't want to leave my vegetarian daughter out. I halved the recipe for the gravy. I used three Morningstar Farms plant based sausage patties. I microwaved them for 30 seconds to defrost them and I crumbled them. I fried them in a splash or two of oil (I used avocado but canola would work too) to give it some oil/fat. Then I just followed the instructions as listed. I'm not vegetarian (my daughter does eat dairy), but it was phenomenal. And I'm never going to buy gravy again. I'm going to use this gravy recipe instead. My daughter agreed and wants me to make this again.

So easy & good! I like my gravy thicker, so I only use 2C of milk & add the other 1/2C milk later for the leftovers, since it thickens up after cooling. Also, I add 1 Tble spoon of butter to the sausage right before I add the flour. Love this recipe!

I fried Swaggerty's sausage patties, removed them from the pan then added the flour. Using a gravy whisk, I made sure the flour cooked for a minute before adding the milk . Used plenty of cracked black pepper and a teaspoon of salt. Stirring constantly, when it began to bubble, I added in 2 of the sausage patties crumbled. Turned out terrific. Ladled on Pillsbury Southern Style Buttermilk biscuits from the freezer section of the store. Good gravy recipe!
The secret sausage gravy ratio is 1/4 cup of flour (Wondra works best), 1/4 cup of fat (butter and or sausage grease) and 2 cups of milk. This is the "golden ratio".

Ever since I started using this recipe years ago, I can't eat anyone else's biscuits and gravy (neither can my kids!) Be prepared to increase the quantity if you have extra people, many will want seconds! Also, stick with Jimmy Dean, (I use the raw ground kind in a tube, HOT is great!) whenever I try a different sausage, I always regret it! I also like to add a couple Tablespoons of butter before the flour. If you're like me and only have skim milk in the fridge, you can add a can of FF evaporated milk to make it creamier! I sometimes make huge batches for big camping parties, Just make at home, freeze in gallon ziplocs and reheat at the campsite (take a big bag of pre-baked bisuits). Good over scrambled eggs too! Tabasco or Cayenne is a nice condiment for me! Try these, you'll find out that it's easy to make gravy!
Its amazing and awesome and very good yummy 😋 😍
So so easy and we love it every time!
Just like the recipe title "easy", it was a family pleaser! We loved it and it will be the go-to when sausage gravy is needed.
Absolutely delicious!!!

Quick and easy to make but not as good as obviously longer to make recipes but it will quickly satisfy your biscuits and gravey crave... just make sure unlike me... you make your own biscuts too.. this is just about the gravey.
So simple and so good! Didn't change a thing. This is the classic recipe I have been looking for!

I love the ingredients in the recipe, and I use this recipe for all of my gravy. I’ve never noticed before in the instructions that you have on here, it doesn’t tell you to cook that roux with the sausage til it’s browned!
Easy and delicious!
Easy and delicious! I add some thyme and sage to it for flavor
